explanation: Y181V reduces nevirapine binding primarily through loss of a critical aromatic interaction; the tyrosine's phenolic ring provides π-stacking or hydrogen-bonding stabilization of the inhibitor that is eliminated when replaced by the smaller, aliphatic valine side chain. The 53.6 Ų volume reduction creates a cavity within the NNRTI pocket core that nevirapine can no longer fully occupy, compromising van der Waals contacts that normally contribute favorable binding energy at the 3.8 Å interfacial distance. This combination of lost polar/aromatic contacts and reduced surface complementarity destabilizes the ligand-protein complex by approximately 1 kcal/mol, sufficient to confer clinically relevant resistance while the mutation maintains overall fold integrity.
